items.summary: India's economy is predicted to grow by 7.6% in the July-September quarter according to economists. Consumer demand has shown resilience, mitigating the effects of rising inflation pressures. Predictions indicate continued strength from passenger vehicle sales and bank credit growth. Despite potential slowdowns in the second half of the fiscal year, investments are expected to improve. The Reserve Bank of India may raise rates as economic conditions evolve.

items.title: China and India mask a growing crisis in global coal
items.summary: Global coal consumption is resilient due to rising demand from China and India, which is increasing despite declining figures elsewhere. However, many coal exporters are struggling financially as they face significant losses in their operations. The coal industry is experiencing tough economic conditions, with job losses and company closures becoming commonplace.

items.title: How India became a rice powerhouse - and why it's becoming a problem
items.summary: India's rice production has significantly increased, bolstered by government subsidies and new crop varieties. This rise in output has led to a surplus that threatens fiscal stability due to high subsidy costs. Political tensions arise between the central and state governments regarding rice pricing and production. While domestic demand is not expected to grow significantly, exports continue to increase.

items.title: Nepal gets nod to import 350 MW of power from India during winter
items.summary: Nepal has gained authorization to import up to 350 MW of electricity from India amid declining hydropower generation. This approval will remain effective from November 17, 2026, until July 31, 2027. The Nepal Electricity Authority can procure electricity through various transmission lines to meet domestic demand. Several hydropower projects have been affected by recent floods, limiting local production capabilities.

items.title: Adani Airport Holdings unveils next-generation Adani Rewards membership across eight airports
items.summary: Adani Airport Holdings has launched an upgraded rewards membership programme across eight airports, offering passengers benefits worth up to Rs 65,000 annually. Integrated with Adani OneApp, the tier-based scheme combines travel, shopping, dining and lounge privileges as the company looks to boost digital transactions and non-aeronautical revenue.

items.title: Mukesh Ambani seeks to build satellite capacity for Starlink challenge
items.summary: Reliance Group is eyeing partnerships for manufacturing a 1,600-satellite broadband network aimed at competing with Starlink. The planned low-earth orbit constellation aims for completion by 2035 to enhance connectivity in India. Reliance is negotiating with both domestic and international manufacturers to support its manufacturing goals.

items.summary: Indian enterprises are moving AI into financial services, retail, supply chains and manufacturing. Survey findings show growing adoption and measurable returns, but data readiness, compliance and organisational change remain significant challenges.

items.title: States' subsidy, cash transfer outgo jumps from 16% to 21% of revenue receipts in 5 years: Report
items.summary: States' spending on subsidies and transfers has risen significantly over recent years and is expected to continue growing. By 2026-27, states are estimated to spend around 1 percent of GDP on cash transfer schemes. Major contributors to this increase are power subsidies and unconditional transfers for various beneficiaries, including women and farmers. States such as Andhra Pradesh and Chhattisgarh are among the highest spenders in these categories.

items.title: ONGC gas leak in Andhra Pradesh's Konaseema forces evacuation of around 800 people
items.summary: A gas leak occurred at an ONGC gas well in Geddada, prompting the evacuation of around 800 residents. Authorities cordoned off a 1 km radius around the well and diverted traffic along National Highway 216. Local officials instructed residents to avoid electrical appliances and gas stoves to prevent ignition. Continuous monitoring revealed zero gas concentration at the assessed locations after the leak began.

items.title: India, Philippines discuss defence, trade ties as PM Modi meets President Marcos Jr.
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. discussed enhancing cooperation in various sectors. They acknowledged the momentum in bilateral relations, particularly in defence and investment areas. The two leaders reflected on their previous meetings, emphasising the importance of their strategic partnership. India aims to expand its engagement with Southeast Asian nations through diverse initiatives.
